Stocks did the pushing: Nasdaq −5.5%, Nasdaq 100 −6.4%; CoinGlass logged over $1B of 24-hour liquidations, mostly longs (CoinDesk, Nov 5).
Spot did not step in: Coinbase premium −0.156% daily, −0.170% 7-day average; ETFs took a provisional +$74.6M on Nov 4, ending three outflow days, but the 7 trading days to Nov 3 are still −$717M.
Bull day 28; the 200-day MA at 73,192 is 3.7% below the close; no exit-framework trigger.

The selling came from collapsing risk appetite in stocks, not crypto-specific news; a −0.156% Coinbase premium and still-positive funding show nobody stepped in to buy spot. findings.title: 70% of short-term coins are at a loss, but short-term holders have not sold at a loss yet
findings.lean_why: Most short-term holders are underwater and their break-even or stop-loss selling has not been released; supply is thin from 74K down to 66K, so price can move fast if 74K gives way.
findings.what: Question: how much latent selling sits below now that price is back at short-term holders' cost? Price fell back to the STH cost basis in one day, putting 70% of short-term coins at a loss on paper, yet those actually selling are still mostly in small profit. Close 75,980 vs STH cost basis 75,989; supply in profit 41.6% → 27.4%; STH-SOPR 1.0015 (Bitview, CheckOnChain, Nov 5).
findings.why: Participants (CheckOnChain actual coin age, Nov 5): short-term holders hold 3.728M BTC at an average cost of 75,344; the thickest buckets are 76K (625K), 80K (614K) and 78K (508K), and the close sits right at the bottom of the thickest one. Thirty days ago (Bitview actual, Oct 4) it was 3.509M at 73,784. Estimated (Oct 4 → Nov 4) new coins concentrated at 80K (561K) and 76K (469K). Cost map: the true market mean at 77,618 is 2.2% above; the thickest LTH supply above the close is 84K (800K BTC). Behavior: STH realized loss 3,834 BTC, +69% in a week, but realized profit of 4,279 still exceeds it (ratio 1.12); STH-SOPR has not fallen below 1, and the last loss-taking low was 0.9918 on Oct 30. Network net realized P/L was +$561M on Nov 4 and −$1.674B over 7 days (CoinMetrics). Contradiction: illiquid supply +1.49% over 7 days (1-year percentile 99.2, Nov 4); coins are moving into dormant wallets, which does not look like panic.
findings.alt: STH-SOPR is daily and about a day late; concentrated selling on the afternoon of Nov 5 may be averaged out by profit-taking earlier that day, so tomorrow's print is more complete. The estimated part (30-day new coins) differs from actual STH totals by 4.4%, with 8.2% misplaced; it is per-UTXO, so exchange wallet consolidation counts as turnover. Bitview and CheckOnChain STH cost differ by about $650, and the 'break' is only $9, so price is effectively on the line.
findings.history: Price crossing below the STH cost basis happened 4 times since 2025-06 (2025-08-30, 09-25, 10-11, 2026-05-17), followed by +3.4%, +2.2%, −6.8% and −15.2% over 30 days, median −2.3% (baseline −0.5%); n=4, too small, background only. Crossing below the true market mean: also 4 times, median −6.5%.
findings.so: Logic chain: those who bought at 76–80K last week are back at cost as a group, so the view that the 76K handover was done (2026-11-04-1) is refuted; but they have not sold at a loss yet, so the real selling is still ahead. Scenario (conditional, CheckOnChain Nov 5): at a 74,000 close 2.588M BTC of short-term coins would be at a loss; at 66,000 that only rises to 2.679M, so supply in between is thin; it jumps to 3.082M at 64,000. In other words, if 74K gives way there is no thick cost zone below until 66K. The market stage and exit framework are unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 12: STH-SOPR below 0.99 means short-term holders are selling at a loss and latent supply has turned into real selling — confirms; a close back above 78,000 (above the thickest pile) refutes.

findings.title: BTC fell with stocks; longs were flushed but funding is still positive
findings.lean_why: The drop came from stocks, nobody stepped in on spot, and leveraged longs have not fully cleared; there is an estimated long-liquidation band below.
findings.what: Stocks dragged this drop and no buyers inside crypto stepped in: the Nasdaq fell 5.5% the same day BTC fell 5.55%; CoinGlass logged over $1B of liquidations, mostly longs, yet weighted funding is still 7.57% (CoinDesk, this site, Nov 5).
findings.why: Who pushed: on the macro side, Nasdaq 100 −6.4%, semiconductors −12%, VIX to 28; BTC's 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq is 0.645 (FRED, Nov 4). Derivatives: funding 8.68% → 7.57%, only slightly lower, with Hyperliquid still at 10.95%; DVOL 38.06 → 42.27 and 25Δ risk reversal −2.88 → −5.57, so more people bought protection, but perp longs did not exit in size. Spot: Coinbase premium −0.156% daily, −0.170% 7-day average, and the 30-day average of −0.137% is the lowest since 2022 (n=1,500); stablecoins −1.84% over 7 days and −$13.2B over 30 days (DefiLlama, Nov 5). The only good news is Asia: the OKX OTC USDT discount closed to zero (snapshot), plus a provisional +$74.6M ETF inflow on Nov 4. Cross-check: CoinDesk reported BTC futures OI below $26B the same day, the lowest since mid-September (Coinalyze), so leverage did shrink; with our funding still positive, the picture is fewer positions, but those left still lean long.
findings.alt: The Coinbase premium only compares Coinbase with Binance and misses CME and ETFs; the Nov 5 ETF flow is not out yet, so flows on the drop day are unknown. Funding covers Deribit, OKX and Hyperliquid; Binance and Bybit are unreadable. Large Hyperliquid accounts may be market makers or hedges. CoinGlass and Coinalyze figures use a different basis from our estimated liquidation bands and are not compared.
findings.history: The prior 6 times the Coinbase premium 7-day average hit the bottom 2% of its year (since 2022-10), the median 30-day return was +8.5% (baseline +2.2%); the prior 4 sharp 7-day stablecoin drops had a median of −5.5% (baseline +1.2%); the two point in opposite directions and n is only 6 and 4, background only.
findings.so: What changed is position: price went from above the mean back to the STH cost basis and the post-election squeeze is fully given back. What did not change is the nature of the buyers: US spot and stablecoins are still leaving, so support now rests on on-chain cost and resting bids ($187M at 75,000), not new money. Conditional: a drop to 73,800–75,100 would trigger a batch of estimated long liquidations (estimate, OKX only), forced selling at market that can speed a decline. The market stage and exit framework are unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 12: a close below 73,800, meaning leveraged longs are forced out and the decline extends — confirms; the Coinbase premium 7-day average back above −0.05%, meaning US spot is buying — refutes.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Idling at Support
items.points: BTC about −10% from the September high, retesting the August breakout; STH supply in profit fell from ≥97.5% to about 38%; true market mean 77.7K, STH cost basis 75.7K, 200-day MA inside the 73–76K band, long liquidation risk at 73–76K and 60–63K; after the past three midterms BTC fell another 15–50% within 2–10 weeks. Conclusion: holding 73–76K is a healthy reset within the August uptrend; a break below 73K points to a longer consolidation.
items.meaning: The Nov 5 close of 75,980 is now at the top of its 73–76K band, where our STH cost basis (75,989) and 200-day MA (73,192) also sit; its 'break below 73K' nearly coincides with our hedge line at 73,192. The midterm history is only 3 cases, so we do not use it for the call.
